 Boston College aims to stay unbeaten at Harvard
 FLM 
 Nov 17, 2026
 A stronger start is one thing Boston College Eagles basketball coach Luke Murray will be looking for when his team visits Harvard Crimson on Wednesday night in Cambridge, Mass.
 The Eagles (4-0) trailed by 11 points four minutes into Sunday's game against New Hampshire before rallying for a 67-55 victory.
 "It's an unacceptable start to the game," said Murray, in his first season as BC's head coach. "I think our guys realized that in the moment (and) responded decently well."
 BC didn't have leading scorer Money Williams against New Hampshire. Williams sustained an undisclosed injury in the second half of BC's victory over Maryland Eastern Shore on Nov. 10 and was listed as day-to-day.
 Williams, a senior guard, is averaging 21.7 points, 6.3 rebounds and 4.3 assists in three games this season.
 Ernest Shelton helped fill the scoring void by tossing in a team-high 17 points against New Hampshire.
 "Money is obviously one of our best players," Shelton said. "Just to step in like that definitely felt right."
 Armoni Zeigler replaced Williams as BC's floor general. He finished the game with 14 points, six rebounds, six assists and two steals.
 "(Zeigler) hasn't had as many reps doing that as Money has," Murray said. "But I give big credit to Armoni. ... He's a real spark plug defensively, (and) did a great job at giving us some life."
 Harvard (2-3) will be trying to end a three-game losing streak. Those losses came against Northeastern (74-70 in OT), George Washington (85-57) and American (70-64).
 Thomas Batties II leads Harvard in scoring (15.8) and rebounding (4.6). Many thought the senior forward might transfer before the season, but Batties said his No. 1 goal is to win an Ivy League championship.
 "I had other offers coming out of high school, but this was the place for me," Batties said. "Gotta finish what I started. ... The program means so much to me."
 Tey Barbour (12.6) and Robert Hinton (11.6) are the other Crimson players scoring in double figures. Barbour, a 6-foot-4 guard, also is second on the team in rebounding (4.2).
